channel.title: Greg Getner — Blog
channel.description: Field notes from 23 years of retention marketing: automations, deliverability, retention, and the expensive mistakes most operators keep making.

item.title: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC: The 20-Minute Deliverability Setup Most Accounts Get Wrong
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: I've audited ActiveCampaign programs where every automation was built correctly, segmentation was tight, and content was strong—but 18% of sends never reached the inbox because nobody had configured DMARC.

item.title: How to Map a Customer Journey in ActiveCampaign From Scratch
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most ActiveCampaign accounts are a graveyard of disconnected automations—each built to solve one problem, none of them talking to each other, all of them firing whether or not the contact should still be receiving them.

item.title: The Win-Back Flow for Lapsed Customers (and When to Give Up)
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most retention programs treat lapsed customers like cold prospects, then wonder why the win-back flow produces unsubscribes instead of orders.

item.title: Using ActiveCampaign Deal Pipelines for Course Cohorts (Not Just Sales)
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most operators treat deal pipelines as a sales-only tool, but they're built to manage any multi-stage process—including the ones happening after someone buys from you.

item.title: The Post-Purchase Sequence Most Ecommerce Brands Never Build
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most ecommerce brands build welcome automations and cart abandonment flows, then wonder why their retention numbers stay flat—meanwhile the entire relationship after purchase runs on default transactional emails and hope.

item.title: The 3-Email Re-Engagement Test I Run Before Unsubscribing Cold Contacts
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most operators either blast cold contacts until they complain or quietly delete them in batches—neither approach improves deliverability, and both leave money on the table.

item.title: How to Build an Abandon Cart Flow That Doesn't Feel Like a Guilt Trip
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most cart abandonment sequences read like the brand got their feelings hurt—but the ones that actually convert lead with utility before they ever mention a discount.

item.title: The Welcome Series Structure That Actually Converts
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Most welcome series are seven generic emails that sound like everyone else's. The ones that convert follow a specific land → check → qualify → offer structure—and never pitch in email one.

item.title: The Hidden ActiveCampaign Features Most Consultants Miss
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: Six ActiveCampaign features I find turned off in almost every account I inherit — conditional content blocks, site tracking, sub-automations, predictive sending, non-sales deal pipelines, and rolling date-field segments.

item.title: Why Your Email List Is Dying (And How to Fix It)
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: A retention marketer's diagnostic for when open rates slide, deliverability drifts, and replies go quiet — plus the four fixes that actually work.

item.title: 5 ActiveCampaign Automation Mistakes That Kill Conversions
item.author: greg@getner.ai (Greg Getner)
item.description: The five ActiveCampaign automation mistakes I find in nearly every audit — goal exits, tag sprawl, no-reply senders, dead contact blasts, and pacing problems — and the specific fixes that recover the conversions they quietly bleed.
